static_traits.name: Fang Ke
static_traits.social_status: Has one supportive friend to confide in, but has not yet shared deep feelings of inferiority; relationship with the supervisor strained by frequent comparison and sense of failure; often comparing with peers and societal success standards at work
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past counseling or therapy experience; no similar psychological problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly and logically; capable of self-reflection and willing to cooperate; presenting strong negative automatic thoughts and catastrophizing tendencies in the report; emotions of anxiety coexisting with hope

basic_info.main_problem: 'I feel I have not achieved anything in life, especially considering my age, which gives me an overwhelming sense of failure and despair.'
basic_info.core_demands: 'I decided to seek counseling because these negative thoughts and feelings have started affecting my mental health and overall well-being.'; 'I need to find a way to cope with these feelings without making the problem worse.'
growth_experiences: Last week learned that a colleague who joined at the same time received a promotion. Compared with others, the client feels career stagnation and falling behind, triggering intense feelings of failure and despair, and questioning self-worth.

A few months ago successfully closed a deal widely considered 'impossible' by colleagues. The client felt proud and competent upon completion, but this positive feeling was quickly diluted by comparison with others.

Over the past year, the client frequently compared with society's standards of peer success, leading to almost daily inferiority, pessimism, and powerlessness, further affecting sleep, self-care, and work motivation.

core_beliefs: I am not as good as my peers (my worth depends on whether I achieve socially recognized accomplishments)

special_situations.event: Learning that a same-cohort colleague was promoted
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not been promoted or achieved comparable accomplishments at this stage, it means I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting unrealistic high goals and over-pressuring oneself to 'catch up' with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have fallen behind; I will not succeed

special_situations.event: Sees others achieve goals or be publicly praised/recognized
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not been recognized, it means I am not important and have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling efforts and using external evaluation as the core standard for judging self-worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never catch up with them

special_situations.event: Comparing age with social success standards (for example, 'at this age one should have reached certain milestones')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: At this age I should already have achieved significant accomplishments, otherwise I am a complete failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Drives oneself with 'must/should' rules and makes highly demanding plans
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: At this age I have not achieved anything; this proves I failed

special_situations.event: The relationship with the supervisor is strained due to self-comparison and a sense of failure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not successful enough, I will disappoint my partner/supervisor, and the relationship will suffer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to recover self-worth and relationship evaluations by raising work requirements and goals

core_conflict.wish: Longing for a sense of achievement of being recognized and seen, proving one's worth
core_conflict.fear: Fears being judged a failure, looked down on by peers and partner, and ultimately rejected or losing important relationships and career opportunities
defense_goal: Maintaining self-esteem and a sense of control by constantly comparing with societal standards and peers and setting excessively high goals, to avoid being seen as a failure

object_relations.self_representation: The loser who was compared and left behind
object_relations.object_representation: Others as judges and standard-bearers of success (colleagues, society, partner)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When peers' achievements or society's success standards for that age are discussed
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Regarding others and society as the judges of one's own value, and presupposing 'I have already been judged a failure'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using analytical language to discuss 'societal standards' and 'milestones', with a steady tone, fewer emotional words, focusing on facts and logic.

manifestations: Repeatedly believing one has not yet achieved anything in life, and the future will not bring success either
Experiencing intense failure and despair after comparing with peers and societal standards
outcomes: Sleep disturbance and difficulty with self-care
Decreased work drive and impaired performance

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses social success standards and age milestones as the absolute criteria for measuring self-worth
Often drives self-demands and goal setting with 'should/must reach a certain achievement'
Treating external recognition as the core basis of worth

exception_events.target_problem: When comparing with peers at work, the client usually feels failure and powerlessness, decreased drive, struggling to maintain good performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few months ago successfully closed a deal widely considered 'impossible', experiencing pride and competence, different from the usual failure narrative.
exception_events.reason: Clue: having a clear challenging goal, increased engagement, and skills put to use, leading to experiences of competence and positive feedback in that situation.

positive_force: Has had notable career achievements (completing a high-difficulty deal)
Willing to seek help and actively cooperate with counseling (positive attitude)
Able to recognize and record one's own achievements to reinforce strengths
negative_force: Negative cognitive tendencies of catastrophizing and predicting the future
Comparison and despair (excessively measuring against peers and societal standards)
Black-and-white standards driven by 'should/must', setting unrealistic high goals
High dependence on external recognition to confirm self-worth
Sleep disturbance and difficulty with self-care leading to further declines in energy and drive

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent self-comparison and catastrophizing (e.g. 'I will never succeed')
antecedent: Seeing colleagues promoted or peers reaching milestones
Seeing others publicly praised or recognized
Thinking about society's success standards for this age
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting societal standards as self-evaluation criteria without digesting them, tightly binding self-worth to external milestones, and making catastrophic inferences and overgeneralizations about the uncertain future
target_behavior.function: Temporarily gaining a sense of control and a self-interpretation framework, trying to push for change through reinforced pressure or avoid facing uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Intensified anxiety and despair, declining work drive and performance, strained intimate relationships, impaired sleep and self-care

target_behavior.behavior: Setting unrealistic high goals and over-pressuring oneself
antecedent: When feeling behind or judged as unsuccessful after comparing with peers
When feeling self-worth threatened after seeing others gain recognition
target_behavior.core_reason: All-or-nothing success standards and 'should / must' rules drive her, attempting through extreme effort to prove value and eliminate the failure label
target_behavior.function: Obtains (or maintains) a sense of self-worth and control, seeking external recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Frequent failures due to excessively high goals; intensified feelings of failure and powerlessness; further worsened sleep and self-care
